test_title: PYST 4: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that he would be moving to the capital soon.

options.text: He said, "I would move to the capital soon."
He said, "I will be moving to the capital soon."
He said, "I shall move to the capital soon."
He said, "I was moving to the capital soon."

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He said, "I will be moving to the capital soon." .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **indirect speech**, and the task is to convert it into **direct speech**.
 
• In indirect speech, the auxiliary verb **"would"** often changes to **"will"** when converting back to direct speech, depending on the context.
 
• The word **"soon"** indicates that the action is expected in the near future, supporting the use of **"will"** in direct speech.

Correct sentence: *He said, "I will be moving to the capital soon."*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I would move to the capital soon" is incorrect because "would" is used for hypothetical situations, not future plans.
 
• **Option 3:** "I shall move to the capital soon" is incorrect because "shall" is rarely used and does not match the tone of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** "I was moving to the capital soon" is incorrect because "was" refers to past continuous, which does not align with the future intent conveyed by "soon."
